title: Orientation-free normal comparison for an etale diagonal map
statement: For smooth separated finite-type maps g:X→Y and h:U→Y of relative dimension d and an etale e:U→X with e≫g=h, construct e×e on self-products, its coefficientwise extended-Rees map, and the induced zero-fibre map n on the actual diagonal normal cones. The square of n with the normal projections and e is Cartesian and carries the zero section to the zero section. Smooth exceptional exchange pulled to zero, together with the canonical site comparison, gives the specified isomorphism normal(h)≅e*normal(g). The definitions selfMap, deformation, normalMap, and normal and the projection/ideal/zero-fibre identities are part of this construction.

proof.text: Form e×e by the pullback universal property. Functoriality of the diagonal ideal gives the coefficientwise Rees map; preservation of t gives its zero-fibre lift.

Use the clopen neighbourhood of the source diagonal from chartGeometry. The flat Cartesian square of centres and the Rees open-composition identity identify the normal-cone lift with a Cartesian normal comparison preserving zero.
Apply the existing smooth exceptional section exchange to that actual Cartesian normal square. Conjugate by the Dnc normal and site comparison isomorphisms.
